events.title: Emperor Augustus
events.description: Octavian, Caesar's adopted son, becomes Rome's first emperor under the name Augustus. He initiates the Pax Romana – a long period of peace that enables the spread of the gospel.

events.title: Roman Census
events.description: Augustus orders a census throughout the empire. Luke links this to Mary and Joseph's journey to Bethlehem. Quirinius is governor of Syria.

events.title: Death of Herod the Great
events.description: Herod the Great dies in Jericho. The kingdom is divided among his three sons: Archelaus (Judea), Antipas (Galilee), and Philip (northeast).

events.title: Emperor Tiberius
events.description: Tiberius succeeds Augustus as emperor. He reigns throughout Jesus' public ministry. The 'emperor's coin' in the Gospels bears his image.

events.title: Pontius Pilate – Prefect of Judea
events.description: Pontius Pilate is appointed as Roman prefect in Judea. His existence is confirmed by an inscription found in Caesarea Maritima in 1961.

events.title: Sejanus' Persecution of the Jews
events.description: Tiberius' advisor Sejanus pursues an anti-Jewish policy in Rome. Jews are expelled from the city. After Sejanus' fall in 31 AD, conditions improve.

events.title: Roman Roads and Infrastructure
events.description: The Roman road network stretches over 400,000 km and binds the empire together. These roads are later used by the apostles to spread the gospel.

events.title: Koine Greek as a Global Language
events.description: Koine Greek is the lingua franca throughout the eastern Mediterranean. The New Testament is written in this language, making it accessible to all educated people.

events.title: Emperor Caligula
events.description: Caligula becomes emperor and demands divine worship. He orders his statue to be erected in the Temple in Jerusalem, but dies before it is carried out.
